definition: Cyc (pronounced SYKE) is a long-term artificial intelligence (AI) project that aims to assemble a comprehensive ontology and knowledge base that spans the basic concepts and rules about how the world works.
details: Hoping to capture common sense knowledge, Cyc focuses on implicit knowledge. The project began in July 1984 at MCC and was developed later by the Cycorp company. The name "Cyc" (from "encyclopedia") is a registered trademark owned by Cycorp. CycL has a publicly released specification, and dozens of HL (Heuristic Level) modules were described in Lenat and Guha's textbook, but the Cyc inference engine code and the full list of HL modules are Cycorp-proprietary.

explainer.lead: Cyc is an attempt to give computers the background knowledge people use without thinking: everyday concepts, facts, and rules about how the world works. By writing that implicit knowledge down, the project aims to help AI systems draw conclusions that would otherwise require every detail to be stated explicitly.

tiers.eli5: Imagine teaching a robot everything you know without ever being told, such as how everyday objects and actions work. Cyc tries to build a giant, organized book of those ideas and rules so the robot can work out some answers itself. Its name comes from “encyclopedia.”
tiers.practitioner: Cyc is applied by representing concepts and common-sense rules in an ontology and knowledge base, with CycL providing a publicly specified representation language. Reasoning depends on the inference engine and Heuristic Level modules, but the engine code and complete module list are Cycorp-proprietary, so it should not be treated as a fully open implementation.
tiers.paperLevel: Cyc can be summarized as (O, KB, R): an ontology O of basic concepts, a knowledge base KB of facts and rules, and reasoning R intended to make implicit common-sense knowledge usable. The project began at MCC in July 1984 and continued at Cycorp; Lenat and Guha’s textbook described dozens of HL modules. The full inference engine code and HL module list remain proprietary.

explainer.example: Suppose the knowledge base says “Alice is a person” and includes a rule that people have heads. The reasoning system can conclude that Alice has a head without anyone entering that specific fact about Alice.

usedIn.name: Common-sense reasoning
usedIn.detail: Represents implicit everyday knowledge so conclusions do not all have to be entered as separate facts.

usedIn.name: Knowledge representation
usedIn.detail: Uses an ontology, a knowledge base, and the CycL language to organize concepts and rules.

usedIn.name: Cycorp
usedIn.detail: The company that continued developing the project after its start at MCC and owns the Cyc trademark.

explainer.intuition: People constantly fill in unstated details when understanding the world, but computers normally need those details supplied. Cyc tries to make that missing background available as a structured collection of concepts and rules.
howItWorks: Identify basic concepts and everyday rules about the world.
Organize the concepts into a comprehensive ontology.
Store facts and rules in a knowledge base using the CycL representation language.
Apply reasoning to combine what is stored and derive conclusions that were not stated directly.
Use specialized Heuristic Level modules to support parts of that reasoning.
explainer.whyItMatters: Cyc tackles a central obstacle in AI: much human knowledge is obvious to people but invisible to machines. Its long-running effort shows what it takes to turn common sense into explicit, machine-usable representations.
misconceptions: Cyc is not merely a collection of explicit facts; its main goal is to capture implicit common-sense knowledge.
Cyc is not fully open: CycL’s specification is public, but the inference engine code and full HL module list are proprietary.
“Cyc” is a registered Cycorp trademark derived from “encyclopedia,” not simply another word for an encyclopedia.
